clue.text: Speculation over how "film noir" was made?

definitions.meaning: a wild guess made without real knowledge
read literally, a film was shot, and noir is French for black, so it was shot in darkness

explanation.surface: A critic speculates about the making of a dark crime movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link word joining the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess made with no information is idiomatically a stab taken blindly in the dark.

clue.text: Speak to conceal tirade from water supplier

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for to conceal gives its sound, spelt here differently

parts.note: to conceal is to hide
a tirade is a rant

explanation.surface: Someone talks to cover up an angry outburst at the water company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speak' marks a sound-alike: the verb for concealing is said aloud, as in Mr Hyde, and the tirade follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire service street valve supplies water for hoses.

clue.text: Uninspiring meat dish

indicators.note: to dish something can mean to spoil or rearrange it, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dull plate of meat at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' rearranges MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and lacking excitement is described as flat or insipid.

clue.text: Students accept poor clue for "core"

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students

indicators.note: poor suggests a badly formed version, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Students put up with a weak crossword clue for the word core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' is the anagram signal and 'accept' the container signal; NUS (the National Union of Students) is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The central part of an atom or cell is its heart or centre.

clue.text: Man finds damaged crate on some land abroad

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a man

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fellow discovers a broken crate on a plot overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' signals the anagram. The unit is metric, used across Europe more than in Britain, hence 'abroad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric measure of area equal to ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: Destiny is to perform to order

parts.note: to perform is to do
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Fate means doing what you are told.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit, an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A grim fate or unavoidable lot awaiting someone.

clue.text: Copy most of answer with one scan inside

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an answer is a reply
one as a Roman numeral is I

indicators.note: inside asks for the inner letters of scan, without its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone copies most of an answer while having a scan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops a final letter and 'inside' asks for the letters between the outer pair of scan; 'Copy' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproduction or exact duplicate of an original object.

clue.text: Main criterion for putting right counter-accusation

indicators.note: putting something right means sorting it out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The chief standard by which errors are corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for putting right' rearranges MAIN CRITERION.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusation made in return against one's accuser.

clue.text: The first serviceman to be our leader?

parts.note: first in rank is prime
a minister conducts a church service, rather than serving in the forces

explanation.surface: Will the top soldier become our national leader?
explanation.walkthrough: 'serviceman' suggests the armed forces, but here it is a clergyman who leads a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the British government is the nation's political chief.

clue.text: Finish with half of them in charge, within a particular region

parts.note: a finish is an end

indicators.note: half of takes the second two of the four letters of them

explanation.surface: Wrap things up with half the group in command of a local area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' them gives EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease or species native to or regularly found in one place only.

clue.text: Axe hospital that's protected by policeman

indicators.note: being protected by means being surrounded, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An axe attack on a hospital guarded by a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts H inside COPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver or hatchet used to chop wood.

clue.text: The track is wide, but not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter of the word is removed

parts.note: wide means broad

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the track is wide, but only at its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' removes B from BROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A street or way for vehicles to travel along.

clue.text: State where meals are taken around ten

indicators.note: around means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: teas are light meals
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A place where dinners are eaten at about ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts TEAS around X, the Roman ten.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the United States, the Lone Star one.

clue.text: Concrete company

definitions.meaning: solid and definite, as a fixed arrangement

explanation.definitionFit: Solid and settled means definite; a business is also a partnership or enterprise.

clue.text: Total crackpot going topless

indicators.note: going topless in a down clue means the top letter is removed

parts.note: a crackpot is a nutter, a mad person

explanation.surface: A complete eccentric strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops N from NUTTER, British slang for a crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete or absolute, as in sheer nonsense.

clue.text: Exclusive firm trapped by bribe

indicators.note: being trapped by means sitting inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: a sop is a small bribe to placate someone
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A special deal: the company is caught in a bribery scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' is the container signal; a sop is something offered to placate, a mild bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A news story published first by one paper alone.

clue.text: Changes for tea — must get dressed

indicators.note: dressed food is prepared and arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People must change their clothes before tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get dressed' rearranges TEA and MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Alters in form, as genes do through mutation.

clue.text: Shout out a demand for alimony?

definitions.meaning: a former spouse asking for payment is an ex making a claim

explanation.surface: A divorced spouse yells for maintenance money.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as EX CLAIM: a claim from an ex.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out suddenly in surprise; the split reading is a former partner's financial demand.

clue.text: Developing source of arum in new perfume

indicators.note: in means this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a perfume is a scent

indicators.note: source of takes the opening letter of arum

explanation.surface: A new fragrance being created from arum lilies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' arum gives A, which 'in' puts inside N + SCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Just coming into being and beginning to grow.

clue.text: Put down roots across a city in America

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to put down roots is to settle

explanation.surface: Settling down somewhere in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts SETTLE around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A major port in Washington State in the US Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Swing section rose with ease, say

indicators.note: rose in a down clue means the word goes upward, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a section is a part

indicators.note: say signals that the next word gives its sound, spelt differently

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EZE

explanation.surface: Part of a rose garden swings easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' turns PART upward to TRAP; 'say' gives EZE, sounding like ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus acrobat's bar hung from ropes is a kind of swing.

clue.text: Divers gents chasing runs in the mist

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows
in means this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a thick mist is fog
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
gents are men

explanation.surface: Gentlemen running after one another through a misty scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like the old word for various, but means people who dive. R goes 'in' FOG, and MEN is 'chasing' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwater swimmers in wetsuits and flippers.

clue.text: Puncture that's impossible at high speed?

parts.note: a puncture is a flat tyre
out means not possible, as in that option is out

explanation.surface: A tyre burst makes driving fast impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: Going as fast as possible, with every effort made.

clue.text: With which one might build a holy city? Never!

parts.note: Mecca is the holy city of Islam
an emphatic no

explanation.surface: Could one construct a sacred city with a toy kit? Never!
explanation.walkthrough: It is a British metal construction toy of strips, nuts and bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's construction kit of metal pieces used to build models.

clue.text: Drop in — create a riot!

definitions.meaning: a drop of liquid from the eye when crying
to rush about wildly or go on a spree

explanation.surface: Pop in and cause chaos!
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word joining the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop shed when weeping; also a wild spree or rampage.

clue.text: A lady is a lady, however viewed

indicators.note: however viewed means it reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: a polite form of address for a lady

explanation.surface: A woman stays a woman from any angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite title for a woman, as in addressing her formally.

clue.text: Religious book or play

definitions.meaning: the book of the New Testament after the Gospels
performs or plays roles on stage

explanation.definitionFit: A New Testament book; also performs dramatically, as an actor does.

clue.text: Volunteers team transport

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
XI is eleven, a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: Volunteers organise transport for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired vehicle for carrying passengers.

clue.text: Pulse, if exhausted

definitions.meaning: a rhythmic throb of the heart

explanation.definitionFit: A rhythm or throb; also worn out, as in dead tired.

clue.text: Offend, but not in anger

parts.note: not in means out
anger is rage

explanation.surface: Someone upsets people while keeping calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock or insult someone deeply.

clue.text: Almost chose to accept period of work

indicators.note: to accept means taking another piece inside
almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: chose means opted
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone nearly decided to take on a stretch of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of the past tense of opt, and 'to accept' makes that trimmed word swallow the period.
explanation.definitionFit: To function or run, as a machine does.

clue.text: Deposit that's tied into means testing

indicators.note: testing hints at trial arrangements, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deposit linked to means-tested benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'testing' rearranges TIED INTO MEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: The settling of particles out of a liquid to form a layer at the bottom.
